We need answer JSON evaluating each story for Problem-oriented criterion. Need understand criterion: violation when story unnecessarily prescribes concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details, algorithms, storage formats, or other solution choices instead of stakeholder need. We need evaluate every story in backlog BC-001 to BC-069. Need return exactly 69 evaluation objects. Need judge only problem-oriented. We can provide evidence and rationale. Need be careful.

We need parse stories. Criterion individual scope. Violation if story unnecessarily prescribes concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details, algorithms, storage formats, or other solution choices instead of stakeholder need. Need identify solution-y stories vs problem.

Backlog has many stories. We need go through each.

Important: Some stories mention specific UI elements like checkbox, WYSIWYG editor, page, link, menu, admin view, URL path, Stripe, payment page, "third step", "second page", etc. These may violate Problem-oriented because prescribe UI solution. But need distinguish concrete UI widgets vs user need. A story should specify problem. However many stories include "so that" and some details.

Let's list all 69 and assess.

We need produce exactly decisions. Let's systematically evaluate.

BC-001: As anonymous user, I want to view a list of sponsors, so that I can thank all awesome sponsors.
Does it prescribe solution? "view a list of sponsors" is a feature/need, not concrete UI widget? A list is a presentation format? Is "list" a concrete UI widget? Problem-oriented says story specifies problem or stakeholder need, not solution. "view a list" could be a UI representation choice but arguably minimal. Lucassen example reimbursement story additionally instructs save button at top right = violation. "view a list" is likely not unnecessary concrete UI widget? Hmm "list" is a UI choice but a common high-level need. QUS operational: Violation when story unnecessarily prescribes concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, implementation details, algorithms, storage formats, or other solution choices instead of stakeholder need. "view a list" might prescribe solution? But all stories with "view a list" are common backlog. Need determine if "list" is concrete UI widget? Could be "a list of sponsors" is necessary info need. It doesn't prescribe how list appears (e.g., table, cards). I'd say No Violation. Evidence "view a list of sponsors". Rationale: list is high-level content need not concrete widget. Confidence High.

BC-002: view a list of user profiles. Similar No violation.

BC-003: As trainingcoordinator, I want to email all the trainers at once from the website for info and updates, so that It is easier to use.
"from the website" prescribes mechanism? But it's stakeholder need: ability to email all trainers at once. "from the website" is context not solution? Maybe not unnecessary. "email all trainers at once" is need. No violation. Could "from the website" be technical mechanism? It's specifying channel, but not concrete implementation. Probably no.

BC-004: As attendee, I want to have a very clear map where the buildings and rooms are, so that I can make it to class on time.
Need is map. Is "map" solution? A map is a representation, but user need is location info. "very clear map" maybe solution-y but acceptable? It doesn't prescribe how to implement map. No violation. However "map" is specific UI artifact. But user need is clear location information; map is a legitimate need. No violation likely.

BC-005: As a trainer, I want to edit my training node myself, so that the training coordinators don't have to and links to slides.
"training node" is Drupal-specific technical term (node), "links to slides" maybe solution. "edit my training node" is implementation detail? It prescribes content type "node" and "links to slides" maybe UI element. Could be violation because "training node" is Drupal technical mechanism. Also "links to slides" is solution. Need decide. The story says "edit my training node myself" rather than need "update my training information". "node" is implementation detail. Violation. Evidence: "training node", "links to slides". Rationale: prescribes Drupal data structure and link UI instead of need to maintain training content/slides. Confidence High. But is "links to slides" part of need? Trainer wants provide slides to trainees; a link is a mechanism. Likely violation.

BC-006: As a trainee, I want to limit to one registration per day per authenticated user, so that we don't have duplicate spaces.
This is a business rule, not solution. No UI prescribed. No violation. Wording "authenticated user" maybe actor not solution. Fine.

BC-007: As trainingcoordinator, I want to have an admin view that helps track registration status for each attendee so that, so that we can see if attendend, refunded, no show.
"admin view" is UI solution? It asks "have an admin view" - concrete UI view. But "track registration status" is need; "admin view" is interface. Could be considered solution choice. QUS violation if concrete UI widgets. "admin view" is not concrete widget but an interface view. It is solution-y? Need determine. They say "admin view that helps track..." not necessarily prescribing specific widget but a view type. Many stories in backlog mention admin view. Operational says concrete UI widgets, technical mechanisms, etc. "Admin view" could be a solution choice (a view). But is it unnecessary? The stakeholder role is training coordinator and need is to track registration status; saying "have an admin view" prescribes presentation as view. Might be borderline. Problem-oriented: A user story specifies problem or need, not solution. "As training coordinator, I want to track registration status for each attendee..." would be problem-oriented; "have an admin view" prescribes UI. Thus violation? Need be consistent.

BC-008: As attendee, I want to be added to a training waitlist, so that so they can be considered for a class.
